text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where team members regularly merge their code changes into a shared repository. The heart of CI is the automated build process: every time someone pushes new code, the system compiles the project automatically. Right after building, the CI pipeline runs a full suite of tests, including unit and integration tests. This means problems like broken code or failing features are caught immediately, often within minutes, instead of being discovered days later. Because issues are detected early, developers can fix them quickly, saving time and reducing frustration. This constant feedback loop keeps the software stable and makes teamwork smoother and more reliable.
